Operating evidence for independent destructive time courses. The Synthetic independent
destructive time course experiment to assess the declared condition target contrasts CM with
CTL. (A) Target-axis recovery probability among replicates with evaluable loading cosine. (B)
Support for the independent condition-by-time estimand among replicates whose target axis was
recovered. Red circles are estimated probabilities; crosses mark either no eligible denominator
or universal downstream model abstention after recovery; hollow triangles mark probabilities
estimated from partial execution. The analysis unit is one independently collected animal; the
design is different biological animals in every retained condition-time cell; complete,
unequal_declared_cells, isolated_library_failure, missing_internal_condition_time_cell; the
estimand is standardized condition-by-time interaction; time is recorded as collection_time
(days 0, 1, 2, 3) in days; adjustment uses batch. 5 deterministic calibration replicates were
requested per design; 29 of 30 executions completed across the displayed designs. Declared cell
sizes and missing observations are retained without imputation or rebalancing. One animal per
condition-time cell; Two animals per condition-time cell; Three animals per condition-time
cell; Unequal one-to-three-animal cells; Three-animal cells with one failed library removes
replicate 3 from CM at day 2; Two-animal cells with one internal cell absent leaves CM at day 2
absent. Recovery uses one absolute loading-cosine threshold of 0.90. This is disclosed
calibration evidence under the shown synthetic regime, not an acceptance result or universal
sample-size rule.
